top_story: Israel’s 12 November strike on Nasser hospital in Khan Younis, which killed a surgeon and other civilians during working hours, further degraded one of southern Gaza’s last critical medical hubs and underscored how the war is collapsing basic civilian survival systems rather than only hitting military targets. That same day in the UK, guilty verdicts against two men who helped surveil journalists for an Iran-linked assassination plot showed Tehran’s coercive reach extending into diaspora communities far beyond the region’s battlefields. By 15 November, Yemeni government forces had retreated from the Bab el-Mandeb area to defend Aden, giving the Houthis a significant battlefield and symbolic gain near a strategic maritime chokepoint. Taken together, these developments point to a regional environment in which armed actors and their state backers are widening pressure on civilians, professionals, and exiled opponents while shifting the balance of insecurity from Gaza’s hospitals to the Red Sea corridor and European exile networks.
